html:
The Western Mono, or Monache, are a Native American people of the western slopes of the Sierra Nevada in central California, along the upper San Joaquin, Kings and Kaweah rivers. They speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, the same as the Eastern Mono across the mountains.

They likely crossed the Sierra from the east some centuries before Europeans came. They gathered acorns, hunted deer and traded over the passes, carrying acorns and baskets east and bringing back obsidian, salt and pine nuts. Their lowland neighbours were the Yokuts, with whom they often married.

The California Gold Rush after 1848 brought miners, ranchers and violence to the foothills. Many Western Mono today belong to rancherias and the North Fork and Dunlap communities.
